scenes.dialogue: Charge sheet filed? That does not mean a full trial. The court must first screen the case, and that screening is where a sharp advocate can win early.
The real question is simple: is there enough material to proceed against your client? If not, discharge.
Under the B N S S, two tools do this screening: discharge and framing of charge. Know the court, section and deadline, and you can spare your client an unnecessary trial.
scenes.shown: Under the BNSS, two tools do this screening: discharge and framing of charge. Know the court, section and deadline, and you can spare your client an unnecessary trial.

scenes.dialogue: What is discharge? The court finds that proceeding against the accused is not justified at this stage.
It is not bail, which concerns liberty while the case continues. And it is not an acquittal after trial either.
Discharge needs judicial consideration and recorded reasons. A denial alone will not get it, and neither will simply filing an application.
Sessions case first. Take an ordinary case committed under Section Two Thirty Two.
scenes.shown: Sessions case first. Take an ordinary case committed under Section 232.

scenes.dialogue: Section Two Fifty lets the accused apply for discharge within sixty days from commitment.
scenes.shown: Section 250 lets the accused apply for discharge within 60 days from commitment.

scenes.dialogue: The Judge considers the record and documents, and hears both sides. No sufficient ground for proceeding? The Judge must discharge the accused, and record reasons.
But if there is ground to presume an offence only a Sessions Court can try, Section Two Fifty One requires a written charge.
scenes.shown: But if there is ground to presume an offence only a Sessions Court can try, Section 251 requires a written charge.

scenes.dialogue: That charge must be framed within sixty days from the first hearing on charge. A different starting point!
scenes.shown: That charge must be framed within 60 days from the first hearing on charge. A different starting point!

scenes.dialogue: Some High Courts treat the sixty day application window as directory. Even so, never gamble on it. File within time.
scenes.shown: Some High Courts treat the 60-day application window as directory. Even so, never gamble on it. File within time.

scenes.dialogue: Different court, different clock. In a Magistrate's warrant case on a police report, Section Two Sixty Two applies.
scenes.shown: Different court, different clock. In a Magistrate's warrant case on a police report, Section 262 applies.

scenes.dialogue: Here the accused may apply for discharge within sixty days from the supply of document copies under Section Two Thirty.
scenes.shown: Here the accused may apply for discharge within 60 days from the supply of document copies under Section 230.

scenes.dialogue: The Magistrate considers the police report and papers, and hears both sides. Charge groundless? The Magistrate must discharge, with reasons.
If the test for proceeding is met, Section Two Sixty Three requires a written charge within sixty days from the first hearing on charge.
scenes.shown: If the test for proceeding is met, Section 263 requires a written charge within 60 days from the first hearing on charge.

scenes.dialogue: This is where advocates slip, so take three dates. A Sessions case is committed on the first of June. That starts its discharge window.
scenes.shown: This is where advocates slip, so take three dates. A Sessions case is committed on 1 June. That starts its discharge window.

scenes.dialogue: In a different case, a Magistrate's warrant case on a police report, copies are supplied on the tenth of June. That starts its own application window.
scenes.shown: In a different case, a Magistrate's warrant case on a police report, copies are supplied on 10 June. That starts its own application window.

scenes.dialogue: If the first hearing on charge is on the first of July, the charge framing period runs from that hearing.
scenes.shown: If the first hearing on charge is on 1 July, the charge-framing period runs from that hearing.

scenes.dialogue: Record the correct trigger for each clock: not the arrest, not the F I R, and never one date for every deadline.
scenes.shown: Record the correct trigger for each clock: not the arrest, not the FIR, and never one date for every deadline.

scenes.dialogue: What does a charge really do? It is the court's formal statement of the offence your client must answer.
Sections Two Thirty Four and Two Thirty Five cover its contents: the offence, the law, the time, the place, and the person involved. Check every particular.
scenes.shown: Sections 234 and 235 cover its contents: the offence, the law, the time, the place, and the person involved. Check every particular.

scenes.dialogue: Under Sections Two Fifty One and Two Sixty Three, the charge is read and explained, and the accused is asked whether he pleads guilty or claims trial.
scenes.shown: Under Sections 251 and 263, the charge is read and explained, and the accused is asked whether he pleads guilty or claims trial.

scenes.dialogue: If he claims trial, the case moves into evidence. A charge does not establish guilt. The prosecution must still prove its case.
What test applies at this stage? Does the material supply a legally sufficient basis to proceed against your client?
Here is the line: strong suspicion founded on the material can justify framing a charge. Proof beyond reasonable doubt belongs to the decision on guilt.
The court must apply its mind, but it should not run a mini trial to decide which witness is truthful.
Equally, a bare accusation without the required legal ingredients is not enough. So test the material against every ingredient.
And the Supreme Court has repeatedly distinguished this screening from deciding guilt.
Picture this: Arjun is accused of stealing Ravi's laptop, worth sixty thousand rupees. Look at two possible files.
scenes.shown: Picture this: Arjun is accused of stealing Ravi's laptop, worth ₹60,000. Look at two possible files.

scenes.dialogue: First file: the prosecution papers, even accepted at face value, contain nothing connecting Arjun to the theft. Argue that the charge is groundless, and seek discharge.
Second file: a witness account and supporting material link him to it. Then a dispute about the witness's reliability may need evidence at trial.
The actual record controls the result, and neither example guarantees an outcome.
One more trap: these sixty day clocks do not fit every case. Warrant cases not started on a police report follow Sections Two Sixty Seven to Two Sixty Nine.
scenes.shown: One more trap: these 60-day clocks do not fit every case. Warrant cases not started on a police report follow Sections 267 to 269.

scenes.dialogue: In summons cases, Section Two Seventy Four generally needs no formal charge. The particulars of the accusation are simply stated to the accused.
scenes.shown: In summons cases, Section 274 generally needs no formal charge. The particulars of the accusation are simply stated to the accused.

scenes.dialogue: But if the accusation is groundless, the Magistrate must record reasons and release the accused. That release then has the effect of a discharge.
Special courts and special statutes may have additional rules of their own. Check them first.
Remember: discharge asks whether the case should proceed. The charge identifies what must be answered. Neither is a finding of guilt.
Your checklist: check the case type, record the correct deadline trigger, and raise your discharge grounds promptly.
Court moving to frame the charge too early? Ask for time, and put your objection on record.
